citations.quote: This generally means that the seller’s practice must be to physically hand eating utensils to its customers, provide utensils necessary to receive the food (such as a bowl at a salad bar or a cup for a fountain soft drink), or include utensils within the packaging that contains the food.

notes: Michigan taxes 'prepared food intended for immediate consumption' (= prepared food: heated, mixed or combined by the seller, or sold with eating utensils the seller provides) and exempts other food. When utensils count as 'provided' changed twice: Treasury Rule 86 (R 205.136) deemed utensils provided by a seller with over 75% prepared-food sales that merely made them available; Emagine (334 Mich App 658, Nov. 19, 2020 per RAB 2026-2) struck that test; 2023 PA 141/142, effective 2024-02-13, put a 'makes available' standard for over-75% sellers into the statute. 2014-03-14 is the effective date of the definitions as amended by 2013 PA 211/2015 PA 171 (retroactive); earlier history not modeled. Michigan has no local sales tax: the 6% state tax is the whole rate, so this MI rule is the entire answer. Plates and cutlery handed to dine-in customers count as utensils provided under every standard in force since 2014, so dine-in service is taxable throughout.

summary: Prewritten software delivered to the customer, on media or by download, is tangible personal property and taxable in Michigan.

citations.quote: "Tangible personal property" means personal property that can be seen, weighed, measured, felt, or touched or that is in any other manner perceptible to the senses and includes electricity, water, gas, steam, and prewritten computer software.

notes: 2004 PA 172/173 added prewritten computer software to 'tangible personal property' effective 2004-09-01 (RAB 2023-10); Michigan taxed canned software before that under earlier guidance (RAB 1999-5), not modeled. summary: Remote access to software hosted by the vendor, with no code delivered to the customer, is not a taxable sale of prewritten software in Michigan.

citations.quote: The majority of the transactions in this case were not taxable under the UTA because they did not involve the delivery of prewritten computer software by any means.

citations.title: Letter Ruling 2019-3 (December 9, 2019)
citations.quote: In summary, the right to access/use prewritten computer software (e.g., cloud computing) will generally not be subject to sales or use tax if the consumer does not receive either a copy of the software program or any part of the program’s computer code.

citations.title: RAB 2023-10, Computer Software and Digital Goods (approved July 31, 2023)
citations.quote: In such cases, the transfer of the software (by subscription or otherwise) does not constitute a taxable retail sale or use of “tangible personal property” (“prewritten computer software”) in Michigan.

notes: Auto-Owners (Mich Ct App, Oct. 27, 2015) set the rule; Treasury's 2016-01-06 notice applied it to all open tax years, so it may reach earlier periods.
